title: Signals & Interactive Terminal Milestone
summary: v1.4 brings FrostVista its first real signal subsystem: the missing half of the process model. Signals give the kernel a mechanism for asynchronous process notification and forced termination, and give the shell a real Ctrl+C. The design follows the Linux RISC-V ABI so that musl-based user programs and the contest runner can use signals unchanged.
scope: This milestone does not aim to implement full POSIX signal semantics, real-time signal queues, `sigaltstack`, `ptrace`, core dumps, per-thread signal masks, or job-control process groups. The goal is a clean, correct signal foundation: delivery, handlers, return, and interactive terminal behavior.

items.title: Process signal state
items.description: `struct Process` gains pending/masked signal sets and a handler table; `fork` copies them.

items.title: Signal primitives
items.description: `signal()` registration and `sigprocmask` basics in a new `kernel/core/signal.c`.

items.title: kill syscall
items.description: locate a pid, set the pending bit, and wake a sleeping target.

items.title: rt_sigpending
items.description: query the pending signal mask from user space.

items.title: Signal delivery checkpoint
items.description: pending signals are checked before returning to user mode via `check_signal()` in `usertrapret`; default actions (terminate, ignore) are handled.

items.title: sigframe & handler entry
items.description: build a RISC-V sigframe on the user stack and enter the handler with the signal number in `a0`.

items.title: sigreturn
items.description: restore the saved trapframe and signal mask from the sigframe and resume the interrupted instruction.

items.title: ABI alignment
items.description: use the RISC-V user stack alignment, handler `a0` argument, restorer return address, and `rt_sigreturn` syscall convention.

items.title: User-side wiring
items.description: `kill()`/`rt_sigaction()`/`rt_sigprocmask()`/`rt_sigpending()` wrappers, terminal input ownership, and the `__restore` stub in the shared user runtime.

items.title: User sleep command
items.description: add the seconds-based `sleep` library wrapper and `/sleep` user application.

items.title: Ctrl+C in fvsh
items.description: the UART Ctrl+C path raises `SIGINT` for registered foreground children while the shell remains alive.

items.title: Faults become signals
items.description: unrecoverable user page faults raise `SIGSEGV` through normal signal delivery instead of panicking the kernel.

items.title: Signal lifecycle
items.description: add a user-space SIGUSR1 raise, delivery, handler, and return-to-workflow round-trip test.

items.title: Ctrl+C shell behavior
items.description: inject a real 0x03 byte, interrupt a sleeping foreground child, verify status 130, and confirm the shell test process survives.

items.title: Fault-to-signal
items.description: an unmapped access terminates only the faulting child with status 139 while its parent and the kernel survive.

validation.command: Existing full suite still passes with signal delivery enabled.
